title: NIST PQC Updates to PIV Working Drafts — Phase 65 GSA post-quantum acquisition review
publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the GSA post-quantum acquisition reporting pack. NIST released preliminary working drafts for adding ML-DSA and ML-KEM support to Personal Identity Verification standards through a proposed dual-stack model.
key_findings: The draft set covers PIV data representation, card command interfaces, and allowed algorithms.
The proposed model retains classical objects while adding new PQC key references and certificate containers.
NIST explicitly labels the materials preliminary rather than formal public drafts.
why_it_matters: Which records move a migration obligation through inventory, solicitation, award, interoperability test, cutover, acceptance, rollback, and legacy retirement? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. The documents convert a high-level federal PQC mandate into inspectable credential and interface changes that vendors and agencies would eventually need to implement.
ftfn_relevance: Adds a concrete technical standards artifact to the migration trail.
Defines formal standards, products, validation, pilots, issuance, and migration as later gates.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The working materials are not final requirements.
They do not prove vendor support, validation, agency pilots, credential issuance, or completed migration.
